cases.sentence: Он знал, что это было глупо, знал, что это даже нехорошо и противно его теперешним ___, но дом этот был целый мир для Левина.
cases.explain: «новым планам» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: The house was big and old-fashioned, and Levin, though he lived alone, had the whole house heated and used. He knew that this was stupid, he knew that it was positively not right, and contrary to his present new plans, but this house was a whole world to Levin. It was the world in which his father and mother had lived and died. They had lived just the life that to Levin seemed the ideal of perfection, and that he had dreamed of beginning with his wife, his family.

cases.sentence: Понятие о ней было для него ___, и будущая жена его должна была быть в его воображении повторением того прелестного, святого идеала женщины, каким была для него мать.
cases.explain: «священным воспоминанием» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Levin scarcely remembered his mother. His conception of her was for him a sacred memory, and his future wife was bound to be in his imagination a repetition of that exquisite, holy ideal of a woman that his mother had been.

cases.sentence: Он вспоминал свои осуждения Тиндалю за его самодовольство в ловкости производства опытов и за то, что ему недостает ___.
cases.explain: «философского взгляда» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: He heard Agafea Mihalovna talking of how Prohor had forgotten his duty to God, and with the money Levin had given him to buy a horse, had been drinking without stopping, and had beaten his wife till he’d half killed her. He listened, and read his book, and recalled the whole train of ideas suggested by his reading. It was Tyndall’s Treatise on Heat. He recalled his own criticisms of Tyndall of his complacent satisfaction in the cleverness of his experiments, and for his lack of philosophic insight. And suddenly there floated into his mind the joyful thought: “In two years’ time I shall have two Dutch cows; Pava herself will perhaps still be alive, a dozen young daughters of Berkoot and the three others—how lovely!”

cases.sentence: И в знак того, что теперь все хорошо и благополучно, она слегка раскрыла рот, почмокала губами и, лучше уложив около старых зуб ___, затихла в блаженном спокойствии.
cases.explain: «липкие губы» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Laska kept poking her head under his hand. He stroked her, and she promptly curled up at his feet, laying her head on a hindpaw. And in token of all now being well and satisfactory, she opened her mouth a little, smacked her lips, and settling her sticky lips more comfortably about her old teeth, she sank into blissful repose. Levin watched all her movements attentively.
